title: California's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: California's 2nd Congressional District, spanning the North Coast from the Golden Gate Bridge to the Oregon border, will hold a general election on November 3, 2026, following a top-two primary on June 2, 2026. The primary narrowed the field from eight candidates to two: seven-term Democratic incumbent Jared Huffman and Republican challenger Robin Littau, a Coast Guard veteran and school board member. The district was redrawn under Proposition 50, and the Cook Political Report rates the general election as Solidly Democratic. Key issues include climate change, environmental protection, wildfire resilience, and federal spending.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the general election were found. The Cook Political Report rated this race as 'Solidly Democratic' prior to the primary.

candidates.name: Jared Huffman
candidates.summary: Jared Huffman is the seven-term Democratic incumbent representing California's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2012. He serves as Ranking Member on the House Natural Resources Committee and also sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. Prior to Congress, he served six years in the California State Assembly, worked as a Senior Attorney for the Natural Resources Defense Council, and served on the Marin Municipal Water District board for twelve years.

candidates.name: Robin Littau
candidates.summary: Robin Littau is a Republican candidate for California's 2nd Congressional District and a member of the Enterprise Elementary School District Board of Trustees. She is a U.S. Coast Guard veteran who served as a diesel mechanic (MK3) aboard the CGC Boutwell and at a search-and-rescue station in Bodega Bay, receiving a life-saving medal and the September 11th medal. Littau is also a small business owner, operating a cleaning company for nearly a decade, and is a Christian mother of four.
